data.description: Common usage corrections for advanced learners
learningPoints: Focuses on grammar patterns commonly influenced by regional English varieties.
Improves control of tense, prepositions, and natural sentence structure.
Builds awareness of global standard English usage.
Strengthens clarity for professional and academic communication.
Helps avoid frequent mistakes in international contexts.
ESOL B1–B2 and aligns with IELTS 5.5–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 60–94 score ranges.

sections.summary: Avoid using present continuous for permanent situations.
sections.explain: Present simple is used for general facts and permanent states.

words.word: I have a large family.
I am having a large family.
I am having large family.

sections.explain: The verb 'return' already implies going back.

words.word: She returned home late at night.
She returned back home late at night.
She came back returned home late.

sections.summary: Avoid adding unnecessary prepositions after certain verbs.
sections.explain: The verb 'discuss' does not require the preposition 'about'.

words.word: We discussed the proposal in detail.
We discussed about the proposal in detail.
We discussed on the proposal.

sections.explain: Misplaced 'only' can change the meaning of a sentence.

words.word: I only asked him for advice.
Only I asked him for advice.
I asked only him advice.

sections.explain: 'Revert' already implies returning to a previous state.

words.word: Please revert to me by tomorrow.
Please revert back to me by tomorrow.
Please revert me back tomorrow.

sections.summary: Use standard expressions for time references.
sections.explain: In standard English we say 'this morning' rather than 'today morning'.

words.word: I met him this morning.
I met him today morning.
I met him in today morning.

sections.summary: Use standard introductions in formal English.
sections.explain: 'Myself Rahul' is a direct translation pattern; standard English uses 'My name is...'.

words.word: My name is Rahul.
Myself Rahul.
Myself is Rahul.

sections.explain: 'Pass out' means faint in international English; 'graduate' is used for education.

words.word: She graduated from university last year.
She passed out from university last year.
She was pass out from university last year.

sections.explain: Standard English uses 'did you understand?' not 'did you understood?'.

words.word: Did you understand the instructions?
Did you understood the instructions?
Did you understanding the instructions?

sections.summary: Use natural phrasing instead of translated structures.
sections.explain: 'Do one thing' is a literal translation pattern not common in standard English.

words.word: Please send me the document later.
You do one thing, send me the document later.
Do one thing, you send me document later.
